 ABC News News Home Multiple flood rescues as heavy rainfall sets in across south-east Queensland Share Share article Multiple flood rescues as heavy rainfall sets in across south-east Queensland
 By Bella Munro
 By Stephen Clarke
 Topic: Weather
 Posted Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 8:29am Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 8:29am Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 8:29am , updated Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 11:27am Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 11:27am Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 11:27am Loading... In short:
 Queensland Police have issued a warning after multiple motorists were rescued from floodwaters by members of the public overnight.
 More than 150mm of rainfall has been recorded in Caboolture, north of Brisbane, as heavy rainfall sets in across large parts of the state.
 What's next?
 Motorists have been advised to be aware of the potential for flash flooding on Friday morning.
 abc.net.au/news/queensland-south-east-storm-warning/107294406 Link copied Share Share article Several people have been rescued from floodwaters overnight as heavy rainfall sets in across central and southern Queensland.
 Almost 140mm fell in the three hour period to 7:30am this morning at Caboolture, north of Brisbane.
 A watch and act prepare to leave warning has been issued for parts of Burpengary and Burpengary East.
 Closer to Brisbane 106mm has so far been recorded at Eatons Hill and almost 50mm in the CBD.
 Two public schools and six independent schools have so far announced they will be closed on Friday.
 For school closures and more localised content, click here. 
 Multiple roads have gone underwater in Burpengary. ( Supplied: City of Moreton Bay ) 
 A severe thunderstorm warning for heavy rainfall and flash flooding has been issued by the bureau for Brisbane, Caboolture, Ipswich, Jimboomba, Boonah and Springbrook.
 Deputy Police Commissioner Chris Stream said people were rescued from floodwaters in two separate incidents.
 "In both cases they've been carried out by other members of the public, and we are receiving a large amount of calls in regards to people being observed driving into floodwaters," Mr Stream said.
 Flooding has closed multiple roads in the Caboolture region north of Brisbane. ( Supplied: Scott Willard ) 
 Flash flooding will be the main risk over the coming days, he said.
 " There is minimal warning so you really need to know the risk where you are. " Senior forecaster Steve Hadley said flash flooding in local creeks could occur over the next few hours.
 "Do have a look around you and keep your situational awareness high today," he said.
 A minor flood warning is in place for the Barcoo River while initial minor flood warnings have been issued for the Bulloo River and the Warrego River.
 Floodwaters inside Morayfield Shopping Centre. ( Supplied: Eye Envy Optometrist )

 Brisbane
 Read more Read more BoM senior forecaster Angus Hines said the thunderstorm is gradually drifting south and has a possibility of heading towards Brisbane's western suburbs and Ipswich later on Thursday morning.
 He said to expect "significant disruption, delays and flooding".
 Already there have been reports of roads flooded in the Rocklea area.
 Moreton Bay
 Read more Read more Senior forecaster Angus Hines said the "very dangerous" thunderstorm was concentrated around the Caboolture-Burpengary area.
 "It has brought incredible amounts of rainfall over about the last three hours," he said.
 "It is pretty likely that that's leading to some really significant flash flooding this morning."
 Mr Hines said the thunderstorm is gradually drifting south and has a possibility of heading towards Brisbane's western suburbs and Ipswich later on Thursday morning.
 He said to expect "significant disruption, delays and flooding".
 Rough sleepers at Wylie Park in Moreton Bay were among the first to feel the impact of the heavy rainfall.
 In a statement Moreton Bay Council said it was sending officers out to the park to assess the impact.
 "We encourage anyone sleeping rough to move out of low-lying areas or sites near creeks or rivers to safer ground," a spokesperson said.
 Queensland's premier said the flooding was further proof parks should not be places of refuge for the homeless — reaffirming his commitment to build 53,500 more social homes by 2044.
 "We don't believe that parks are the best place for people to be," the premier said.
 "Parks are for families to go and enjoy themselves"
 His comments come after Economic Development Queensland issued a show cause notice to Moreton Bay City Council over its "illegal" use of the park for the homeless.
 Scenic Rim
 Read more Read more A Scenic Rim councillor said heavy overnight falls in the region are helping to boost water supplies after months of drier conditions.
 The weather bureau has recorded about 100mm of rainfall at Canungra in the last 24-hours, with more wet weather anticipated.
 Area councillor Stephen Moriarty said creek levels are up, and conditions could change rapidly but for now, the rainfall is welcome.
 "Oh, it makes an amazing difference," Cr Moriarty said.
 "We have so many people who aren't on reticulated water and rely on rainwater for their water tanks, and I know a lot of people have started buying water recently. We love the rain."
 South-west Queensland
 Read more Read more After parts of south-west Queensland were drought-declared this July, the region has finally received a heavy downpour, with ongoing storms expected in the coming days.
 Based on a property in Muckadilla, about 520 kilometres west of Brisbane, crop farmer Scott Loughnan said he had not seen rain this heavy since 2016.
 He said he recorded more than 160mm of rain on his property in the past week.
 "If we have another 40mm, I think that will double what rain we've had for the year," he said.
 "There's a lot of graziers around here, and it [the drought] was pretty dire for them. They were all making plans for feeding livestock and destocking, so this [rain] will make that a lot easier for them."
 Mr Loughnan said while the rain was a relief to many graziers, it came at a bad time for grain growers, who were in the middle of harvesting.
 "This has cost us personally, half a million dollars or more, in lost income," he said.
 "I think the damage has been done to the crops. [The] chickpeas might be salvageable, but I can't change the weather."
